help.tip.label: Tip
help.pick.label: Log label for the examples
help.source.sql.holds: This source holds tables: rows of records, each with the same columns. You ask for data in SQL: SELECT the columns you want FROM a table, keep matching rows with WHERE, and count or sum with GROUP BY. Pick a table and start with one of these.
help.source.sql.time: Time range: $__timeFilter(column) keeps the rows whose time column lies in the range picked at the top; $__timeFrom and $__timeTo are its edges, $__interval a step that fits the chart.
help.source.sql.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, $name puts a variable’s value into the query as a value, never as text, and a list fits into IN ($name). Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.sql.tip: Add WHERE after FROM to keep only the rows you need. The cheat sheet ({keys}) shows filters, sorting and counting.
help.source.promql.holds: This source holds metrics: numbers measured over time, each series named by a metric and its labels (job, instance). You ask in PromQL: the metric’s name alone shows its series; functions such as rate and sum turn them into the view you need.
help.source.promql.time: Time range: every query runs over the range picked at the top, one point per step. [$__rate_interval] and [$__interval] are windows that fit that step.
help.source.promql.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, $name in a label matcher takes the variable’s value, for example job=~$job in braces. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.promql.tip: Narrow a metric to some series with labels in braces, such as job and the value you want. The cheat sheet ({keys}) has more patterns.
help.source.influx.holds: This source holds measurements: points in time with fields (the numbers) and tags (names such as host). InfluxQL reads like SQL: SELECT a field FROM a measurement, with the time range as WHERE $__timeFilter.
help.source.influx.time: Time range: $__timeFilter keeps the points in the range picked at the top; GROUP BY time($__interval) makes one point per step. In Flux, v.timeRangeStart and v.timeRangeStop are its edges.
help.source.influx.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, $name in a quoted tag value takes the variable’s value. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.influx.tip: GROUP BY time($__interval) turns raw points into one value per step, which charts read best. The cheat sheet ({keys}) has more.
help.source.logql.holds: This source holds log lines in streams, each stream named by labels such as job or app. A LogQL query starts with a stream selector in braces, then filters lines by their text; metric queries count lines over time.
help.source.logql.time: Time range: log queries return the lines in the range picked at the top, up to the line limit; [$__interval] is a window that fits the chart’s step.
help.source.logql.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, $name in a label matcher takes the variable’s value. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.logql.tip: Add a line filter after the selector, such as |= followed by a word in quotes, to keep only lines that contain it. The cheat sheet ({keys}) has more.
help.source.search.holds: This source holds documents in indices, each document a set of fields. Search with Lucene text (a word, or field:value), or switch to Query DSL for counts per value and buckets over time.
help.source.search.time: Time range: each search keeps the documents whose time field lies in the range picked at the top; set the time field in the query when the index uses another one.
help.source.search.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, $name in Lucene text becomes a quoted phrase with the variable’s value. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.search.tip: Search one field with field:value, and combine terms with AND and OR. The cheat sheet ({keys}) has ranges and wildcards.
help.source.mongo.holds: This source holds documents in collections; a document can nest objects and lists. You ask with a pipeline: a list of stages that run in order, such as $match to filter, $group to count and $sort, then $limit.
help.source.mongo.time: Time range: the key $__timeFilter with a field name in a $match stage keeps the documents whose date lies in the range picked at the top.
help.source.mongo.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, a string that is exactly ${name} takes the variable’s value, also a list for $in. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.mongo.tip: Put a $match stage first to keep only the documents you need; it also makes the pipeline faster. The cheat sheet ({keys}) has more stages.
help.source.cypher.holds: This source holds a graph: nodes with labels (such as Person) and properties, joined by edges with a type. In Cypher you draw what you look for: MATCH (n:Label) finds nodes, (a)-[r]->(b) follows edges, RETURN says what to show.
help.source.cypher.time: Time range: $__timeFrom and $__timeTo are the edges of the range picked at the top, as date and time values; compare a time property with them in WHERE.
help.source.cypher.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, $name is a Cypher parameter with the variable’s value, so values never become part of the text. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.cypher.tip: Add WHERE after MATCH to keep only some nodes, for example by a property. The cheat sheet ({keys}) shows filters, counts and paths.
help.source.gsql.holds: This source holds a graph: nodes of a type with attributes, joined by edges of a type. Explore runs GSQL as one interpreted query for the source’s graph, or an installed query by its name.
help.source.gsql.time: Time range: GSQL has no time macros. Declare a DATETIME parameter in an installed query and filter on it; a dashboard fills parameters from variables of the same name.
help.source.gsql.variables: Variables: write no $name into GSQL code. Declare query parameters instead; on a dashboard each takes the variable of its name. Explore has no variables, so try a fixed value here first.
help.source.gsql.tip: A SELECT from Start:s -(EdgeType:e)- :t follows edges from a set of nodes to their neighbours. The cheat sheet ({keys}) has more.
help.source.file.holds: This source reads one CSV or JSON file, always as a whole: there is no query language to learn. Read the file, then shape the result with steps on the right: group and count, calculate fields, keep a projection.
help.source.file.time: Time range: a file is read whole; the range picked at the top does not filter it. Charts still show its time column within the range.
help.source.file.variables: Variables: a file query takes none; use steps to filter by a value.
help.source.file.tip: Steps on the right group, count and calculate on this result without writing a query.
help.source.http.holds: This source requests JSON from one web address and reads the answer as documents. A query can add a path below the address, query parameters and where the documents are in the answer; there is no other language to learn.
help.source.http.time: Time range: the source answers what its address returns; the range picked at the top is not sent unless a parameter takes it.
help.source.http.variables: Variables: on a dashboard, a parameter whose value is exactly $name takes the variable’s value.
help.source.http.tip: Steps on the right reshape the documents into a table without writing a query.
help.source.plugin.holds: This source comes from a plugin. Its query is a JSON object whose fields the plugin defines; its own documentation names them.
help.source.plugin.time: Time range: the plugin decides how the range picked at the top applies.
help.source.plugin.variables: Variables: the plugin decides how variables apply.
help.source.plugin.tip: Inspect next to the result shows the query that ran and what came back.

help.starter.promql.rate: Rate of a metric over time

help.starter.logql.latest: Latest 100 log lines of a stream
help.starter.logql.errors: Latest log lines with an error
help.starter.logql.byLevel: Log lines over time per label value
help.starter.mongo.latest: Latest documents in the time range
help.starter.cypher.paths: Paths of up to three steps
help.starter.gsql.neighbours: Show neighbours along an edge type
help.starter.gsql.count: Count the nodes of a type
help.cheat.sql.order.title: The order of the parts
help.cheat.sql.order.text: A query is written in this order; leave out what you do not need. Only SELECT and FROM are required.
help.cheat.sql.rows.title: Every column, first rows
help.cheat.sql.rows.text: * means every column. Keep a row limit while you look around.
help.cheat.sql.columns.title: Some columns
help.cheat.sql.columns.text: Name the columns you want, separated by commas.
help.cheat.sql.where.title: Keep matching rows
help.cheat.sql.where.text: WHERE keeps the rows that match. Text goes in single quotes, numbers without.
help.cheat.sql.like.title: Find text in a column
help.cheat.sql.like.text: LIKE with % matches any text before or after the part you look for.
help.cheat.sql.and.title: Several conditions
help.cheat.sql.and.text: IN lists allowed values; AND needs both conditions, OR either. IS NULL finds empty values.
help.cheat.sql.orderBy.title: Sort
help.cheat.sql.orderBy.text: ORDER BY sorts; DESC puts the highest or newest first.
help.cheat.sql.top.title: Top ten
help.cheat.sql.top.text: Sort, then limit: the ten rows with the highest value.
help.cheat.sql.groupBy.title: Count and sum per value
help.cheat.sql.groupBy.text: GROUP BY makes one row per value; COUNT(*) counts its rows, SUM adds up a column.
help.cheat.sql.distinct.title: Each value once
help.cheat.sql.distinct.text: DISTINCT lists the different values of a column.
help.cheat.sql.join.title: Join two tables
help.cheat.sql.join.text: JOIN puts rows of two tables side by side where the ON condition matches, usually an id.
help.cheat.sql.timeFilter.title: Rows in the time range
help.cheat.sql.timeFilter.text: $__timeFilter(column) keeps the rows in the range picked at the top.
help.cheat.sql.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.sql.variable.text: On a dashboard the variable’s values take the place of $name. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.promql.selector.title: A metric’s series
help.cheat.promql.selector.text: The metric’s name alone returns every series of it.
help.cheat.promql.match.title: Series with a label value
help.cheat.promql.match.text: Labels in braces keep the series that match; = is exact, != excludes.
help.cheat.promql.regex.title: Several label values
help.cheat.promql.regex.text: =~ matches a regular expression; a|b is either value.
help.cheat.promql.compare.title: Only some values
help.cheat.promql.compare.text: A comparison keeps the points that pass it.
help.cheat.promql.topk.title: The highest series
help.cheat.promql.topk.text: topk keeps the k series with the highest values at each step.
help.cheat.promql.sort.title: Sort
help.cheat.promql.sort.text: sort_desc sorts the series of an instant query by value.
help.cheat.promql.sumBy.title: Sum per label
help.cheat.promql.sumBy.text: sum by (label) adds the series up into one per label value.
help.cheat.promql.count.title: Count series per label
help.cheat.promql.count.text: count by (label) says how many series each label value has.
help.cheat.promql.rate.title: Per second, from a counter
help.cheat.promql.rate.text: rate turns an ever-growing counter into a value per second over a window.
help.cheat.promql.avgOverTime.title: Average over a window
help.cheat.promql.avgOverTime.text: avg_over_time smooths a gauge over the window in brackets.
help.cheat.promql.ratio.title: Share of errors
help.cheat.promql.ratio.text: Dividing two sums gives a ratio, here of the requests with a 5xx status.
help.cheat.promql.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.promql.variable.text: On a dashboard the variable’s values take the place of $name. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.influx.select.title: A field in the time range
help.cheat.influx.select.text: SELECT a field FROM a measurement; $__timeFilter keeps the range picked at the top.
help.cheat.influx.where.title: Points with a tag value
help.cheat.influx.where.text: Tags are compared with = and a value in single quotes.
help.cheat.influx.orderBy.title: Newest first
help.cheat.influx.orderBy.text: ORDER BY time DESC with a limit shows the latest points.
help.cheat.influx.groupBy.title: One value per tag
help.cheat.influx.groupBy.text: GROUP BY a tag makes one series per tag value.
help.cheat.influx.timeBuckets.title: One point per step
help.cheat.influx.timeBuckets.text: GROUP BY time($__interval) with mean, max or sum gives one value per step.
help.cheat.influx.flux.title: The same in Flux
help.cheat.influx.flux.text: Flux pipes data through functions with |>. Choose Flux as the language above the editor to use it.
help.cheat.influx.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.influx.variable.text: On a dashboard the variable’s value takes the place of $name. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.logql.selector.title: A stream
help.cheat.logql.selector.text: Labels in braces pick the streams; at least one needs an exact value.
help.cheat.logql.contains.title: Lines with a word
help.cheat.logql.contains.text: |= keeps lines that contain the text; |~ takes a regular expression.
help.cheat.logql.excludes.title: Lines without a word
help.cheat.logql.excludes.text: != drops lines that contain the text.
help.cheat.logql.json.title: Filter by a field of JSON lines
help.cheat.logql.json.text: | json reads each line’s fields; then compare a field like a label.
help.cheat.logql.count.title: Lines per value over time
help.cheat.logql.count.text: count_over_time counts lines per window; sum by groups them.
help.cheat.logql.rate.title: Lines per second
help.cheat.logql.rate.text: rate gives the lines per second over each window.
help.cheat.logql.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.logql.variable.text: On a dashboard the variable’s values take the place of $name. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.search.all.title: Every document
help.cheat.search.all.text: An empty search, or *, matches every document in the time range.
help.cheat.search.field.title: A field with a value
help.cheat.search.field.text: field:value keeps documents whose field has the value.
help.cheat.search.bool.title: Either value
help.cheat.search.bool.text: OR needs either term, AND both; NOT excludes one.
help.cheat.search.range.title: A range of numbers
help.cheat.search.range.text: Compare with >, >=, < and <=, or write a range as [10 TO 20].
help.cheat.search.exists.title: Documents that have a field
help.cheat.search.exists.text: _exists_ keeps documents where the field is set.
help.cheat.search.wildcard.title: Part of a word
help.cheat.search.wildcard.text: * stands for any letters at the end of a word.
help.cheat.search.sort.title: Sort and limit
help.cheat.search.sort.text: In Query DSL, sort orders the hits and size limits them.
help.cheat.search.terms.title: Count per value
help.cheat.search.terms.text: A terms aggregation counts documents per value of a keyword field.
help.cheat.search.histogram.title: Documents over time
help.cheat.search.histogram.text: A date histogram counts documents per step; $__interval fits the chart.
help.cheat.search.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.search.variable.text: On a dashboard the variable’s value takes the place of $name. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.mongo.limit.title: The first documents
help.cheat.mongo.limit.text: $limit keeps the first documents; keep one while you look around.
help.cheat.mongo.match.title: Keep matching documents
help.cheat.mongo.match.text: $match keeps documents whose fields have the values given.
help.cheat.mongo.in.title: Several conditions
help.cheat.mongo.in.text: $in lists allowed values; $gt, $gte, $lt and $lte compare numbers and dates.
help.cheat.mongo.project.title: Some fields
help.cheat.mongo.project.text: $project with 1 keeps a field, 0 drops it.
help.cheat.mongo.sort.title: Sort
help.cheat.mongo.sort.text: $sort with -1 puts the highest or newest first, 1 the lowest.
help.cheat.mongo.group.title: Count and sum per value
help.cheat.mongo.group.text: $group makes one document per _id; $sum with 1 counts, with a field adds it up.
help.cheat.mongo.lookup.title: Join another collection
help.cheat.mongo.lookup.text: $lookup adds the matching documents of another collection as a list.
help.cheat.mongo.time.title: Documents in the time range
help.cheat.mongo.time.text: $__timeFilter with a date field keeps the range picked at the top.
help.cheat.mongo.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.mongo.variable.text: On a dashboard the variable’s value takes the place of ${name}. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.cypher.match.title: Nodes with a label
help.cheat.cypher.match.text: MATCH finds what the pattern draws; RETURN shows it, LIMIT keeps it small.
help.cheat.cypher.where.title: Nodes with a property value
help.cheat.cypher.where.text: WHERE keeps the matches whose property has the value.
help.cheat.cypher.contains.title: Find text in a property
help.cheat.cypher.contains.text: CONTAINS, STARTS WITH and ENDS WITH compare parts of text.
help.cheat.cypher.orderBy.title: Sort
help.cheat.cypher.orderBy.text: ORDER BY sorts what RETURN shows; DESC puts the highest first.
help.cheat.cypher.count.title: Count per value
help.cheat.cypher.count.text: count(*) next to another value counts the matches per value.
help.cheat.cypher.traverse.title: Follow edges
help.cheat.cypher.traverse.text: -[r:TYPE]-> follows edges of a type in their direction; leave out > for both directions.
help.cheat.cypher.degree.title: Most connected nodes
help.cheat.cypher.degree.text: Counting the edges of each node finds the ones with the most.
help.cheat.cypher.path.title: Shortest path
help.cheat.cypher.path.text: shortestPath finds the shortest way between two nodes, here up to five steps.
help.cheat.cypher.time.title: Nodes in the time range
help.cheat.cypher.time.text: Compare a time property with $__timeFrom and $__timeTo.
help.cheat.cypher.variable.title: A dashboard variable
help.cheat.cypher.variable.text: On a dashboard $name is a parameter with the variable’s value. It does not run in Explore, which has no variables.
help.cheat.gsql.select.title: Nodes of a type
help.cheat.gsql.select.text: A set of nodes, a SELECT from it, then PRINT what to show.
help.cheat.gsql.where.title: Nodes with an attribute value
help.cheat.gsql.where.text: WHERE keeps the nodes whose attribute has the value; compare with ==.
help.cheat.gsql.orderBy.title: Sort
help.cheat.gsql.orderBy.text: ORDER BY with LIMIT keeps the first nodes in that order.
help.cheat.gsql.accum.title: Count edges per node
help.cheat.gsql.accum.text: An accumulator (@degree) collects a value per node while the SELECT follows edges.
help.cheat.gsql.traverse.title: Follow edges
help.cheat.gsql.traverse.text: -(Type:e)- follows edges of a type from the start nodes to their neighbours.
help.hint.readOnly: Data sources are only read in Kalzit, so the query must only read too: one SELECT (or a MATCH with RETURN, a pipeline without $out). Start from a reading example in the cheat sheet.
help.hint.timeout: The query took too long. Pick a shorter time range at the top, add a time filter or a row limit, and try again.
help.hint.variable: The query uses the variable {name}, but Explore has no variables. Put a fixed value in its place to try it here.
help.hint.timeFilter: The time filter needs the name of a time column (or field) in its brackets.
help.hint.unclosed: Something opened in the query is not closed: a quote, a bracket or a comment. Check the end of the query.
help.hint.empty: The query is empty. Write one, or start from one of the examples.
help.hint.syntax: The database could not read the query near {name}. Look for a missing comma, quote or bracket just before it, and compare with the basics in the cheat sheet.
help.hint.syntaxPlain: The database could not read the query. Look for a missing comma, quote or bracket, and compare with the basics in the cheat sheet.
help.hint.unknownTable: There is no table {name} in this source, or it is in another schema. The schema list shows the tables you can query.
help.hint.unknownColumn: There is no column {name} in the table queried. The schema list shows each table’s columns.
help.hint.unknownFunction: The source knows no function {name}. Check its spelling; the cheat sheet shows common ones.
help.hint.influxLanguage: This InfluxDB version does not answer that language. Choose another one above the editor: InfluxQL works on every version.
help.hint.influxDatabase: The source names no database or bucket, so the query has nothing to read. An admin can set it in the source’s settings.
help.hint.logqlSelector: A LogQL query needs at least one label with an exact value in braces before any filter, such as job and its value.
help.hint.unknownIndex: There is no index {name} in this source. The schema list shows the indices you can search.
help.hint.mongoCollection: Pick a collection of this source; system collections cannot be read.
help.hint.mongoStage: That stage or operator is not allowed, because it could write data or run code. The cheat sheet shows the stages for reading.
help.hint.mongoArray: A pipeline is a list of stages in square brackets, each stage an object in braces.
help.hint.cypherVariable: The query uses a name that no MATCH defined. Each name in RETURN or WHERE must come from the pattern.
help.hint.gsqlGraph: An interpreted query must name the source’s own graph after FOR GRAPH.
help.hint.gsqlVariable: Write no $name into GSQL code; declare a query parameter instead.
help.hint.fileFormat: The file could not be read in its format. Check that it is valid CSV or JSON, and the format in the source’s settings.
help.hint.httpDocumentsPath: The documents path does not lead to anything in the answer. Leave it empty to see the whole answer, then pick the part with the documents.
help.hint.httpStatus: The address did not answer with JSON. Check the path, and Inspect for what came back.
help.hint.rowLimit: The result stopped at the row limit, so it shows only part of the data. Add a time filter or a row limit to the query; the cheat sheet shows how.
